# Attributes

::: {.callout-note appearance="default" collapse="false"}
Q: What is this `[...]` thing that appears above the methods in C#?
:::


Those `[...]` things above methods (and classes, properties, etc.) in C# are called **Attributes**. Since you're familiar with Dart, they're similar to annotations in Dart (the `@` syntax).

## What are Attributes?

Attributes are metadata tags that provide declarative information about your code elements. They don't directly change the behavior of the code, but they provide information that can be used by:
- The compiler
- The runtime
- Other tools (like analyzers, serializers, etc.)

## Basic Syntax Comparison

```csharp
// C# - Using Attributes
[Obsolete("Use NewMethod instead")]
[HttpGet]
public string OldMethod() 
{
    return "Hello";
}
```

```dart
// Dart - Using Annotations (your familiar syntax)
@deprecated
@override
String oldMethod() {
    return "Hello";
}
```

## Common C# Attributes

Here's a simple diagram showing attribute usage:

```
                 ┌─────────────────┐
                 │   [Attribute]   │
                 └────────┬────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
            ┌──────────────────────────┐
            │   Target (Class/Method/  │
            │   Property/Field/etc.)   │
            └──────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. **System Attributes**
```csharp
// Mark something as obsolete
[Obsolete("This method is deprecated. Use CalculateV2 instead.")]
public int Calculate() { }

// Conditional compilation
[Conditional("DEBUG")]
public void DebugLog(string message) { }

// Serialization
[Serializable]
public class Person { }
```

### 2. **ASP.NET Core Attributes** (for web APIs)
```csharp
[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class UsersController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult GetAll() { }
    
    [HttpPost]
    [Authorize]
    public IActionResult Create([FromBody] User user) { }
}
```

### 3. **Data Validation Attributes**
```csharp
public class User
{
    [Required]
    [StringLength(100)]
    public string Name { get; set; }
    
    [Range(18, 120)]
    public int Age { get; set; }
    
    [EmailAddress]
    public string Email { get; set; }
}
```

## Creating Custom Attributes

You can even create your own attributes:

```csharp
// Define a custom attribute
public class AuthorAttribute : Attribute
{
    public string Name { get; }
    public string Date { get; }
    
    public AuthorAttribute(string name, string date)
    {
        Name = name;
        Date = date;
    }
}

// Use your custom attribute
[Author("Dr. Smith", "2024-01-15")]
public class MedicalImageProcessor
{
    // Your radiology AI code here
}
```

## Attribute Parameters

Attributes can have:
- **Positional parameters** (required)
- **Named parameters** (optional)

```csharp
// Positional parameter: "message"
// Named parameter: DiagnosticId
[Obsolete("Use new API", DiagnosticId = "DIAG001")]
public void OldMethod() { }
```

## Practical Example for Your Domain

Since you work with radiology AI, here's a relevant example:

```csharp
public class DicomImage
{
    [Required]
    [RegularExpression(@"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+")]  // DICOM UID pattern
    public string StudyInstanceUID { get; set; }
    
    [Range(0, 4095)]  // 12-bit grayscale range
    public int PixelValue { get; set; }
    
    [JsonPropertyName("modality")]  // JSON serialization
    public string Modality { get; set; }  // CT, MR, CR, etc.
}
```

## Try It Yourself

Create a simple console app to experiment:

```csharp
using System;
using System.Diagnostics;

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        TestMethod();
        DebugOnlyMethod();
    }
    
    [Obsolete("Just for testing")]
    static void TestMethod()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("This method is obsolete!");
    }
    
    [Conditional("DEBUG")]
    static void DebugOnlyMethod()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("This only runs in DEBUG mode");
    }
}
```

When you compile this, you'll see a warning for the obsolete method, and `DebugOnlyMethod` will only execute when building in DEBUG configuration.
